stories.title: AI CEOs call for industry slowdown
stories.summary: Anthropic's Dario Amodei and OpenAI's Sam Altman are joining calls for a slowdown amid fears the AI industry is racing toward building technology that humans can't control.

stories.title: Why Somali pirate attacks are ramping up again
stories.summary: NPR's Elissa Nadworny speaks with Federico Varese, a professor at Sciences Po who studies Somalia's maritime criminal gangs, about why attacks on ships off Somalia's coast are on the rise again.

stories.title: Ringing in the Jewish new year with a twist on a Rosh Hashanah classic
stories.summary: Pati Jinich is a renowned chef and cookbook author. She was born in Mexico to a Jewish family, and her marzipan-stuffed challah bread blends her cultures in an exciting and delicious way.

stories.title: Palestinian author's secret effort to preserve his works about life under occupation
stories.summary: Palestinian author Raja Shehadeh has secretly sent his archives from the Israeli-occupied West Bank to Scotland, worried they could be destroyed in an Israeli military raid.

stories.title: Trump's visit to Ireland for the Irish Open tees off with diplomatic controversy
stories.summary: President Trump heads to his golf club in Doonbeg while working in some Irish diplomacy.

stories.title: How China tried to control the narrative on the devastating floods in Nepal and Tibet
stories.summary: Reporting over so-called "the Great Firewall," a journalist details how to report for a global audience from Beijing despite tight obstacles imposed by the government.
